simple.meaning: גָּלַע (gâlaʻ) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to be obstinate.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 3 times in Proverbs, beginning at Proverbs 17:14. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גָּלַע (H1566) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: גָּלַע (gâlaʻ) / H1566 is traced through Proverbs 17:14, Proverbs 18:1, Proverbs 20:3 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H1566. gala [ גָּלַע ] verb expose, lay bare (Late Hebrew Pi`el disclose, make known ; compare Arabic (Frey) a. exuit (vestem), removit (praeputium); nuda fuit (femina); b. patuit (os) labiis non tegentibus dentes; impudica fuit (mulier); compare also Syriac circumcise (in Lexicons); Ethiopic cortex, crusta, testa ; Gr Monatsschr. 1884, 24 f. ; Schult Thes De Prov 17:14 Fl in De, Now Str & most derive Hebrew meaning from Arabic b ; shew the teeth , then snarl, quarrel (compare Arabic conjugation III), but see Gr l.c .) — Hithpa`el Perfect הִתְגַּלַּע Prov 17:14 ; Imperfect יִתְגַּלָּ֑ע 18:1 ; 20:3 ; — disclose oneself, break out, 17:14 subject רִיב ; break or burst out in contention, strife 20:3 subject כָּלאֱֿוִיל ; similarly 18:1 (followed by בְּ against ; Gr l.c. proposes יִלְעַג or יַלְעִיג ). גַּלְעֵד see below II. גלל .
